brief: UBS argues 2026's ~20% S&P 500 forward P/E derating, despite ~33% EPS growth, sets up a favorable 2027: after a >10% P/E decline, SPX has historically returned a median 20% as roughly 30% of the derating reverses. It forecasts 2027 SPX EPS of $430 (+18%) and 2028 EPS of $490 (+14%), with NVDA, MU and AVGO alone driving ~45% of 2027's growth, and keeps its end-2027 target at 8900 (18x 2028 EPS) while setting an end-2028 target of 9600. The AI capex case rests on $6-8tr of cumulative 2025-30 spending needing $2-4tr of revenue, against UBS's ~$2.5tr demand estimate, so it buys Semis and Software despite the selloff, funded from Tech Hardware. Expecting two more Fed hikes and rates staying elevated, UBS favors Financials and NDX over RTY and is underweight High Leverage. State-level pauses after the midterms threaten ~30% of 2028 data-center capacity, a risk to 2028 EPS but not 2027's. Net buybacks, down ~$120bn Q1-Q3 as hyperscalers swung to issuing stock, are forecast to rebound $200-400bn in 2027.
